sanskrit: praṇavaṃ mātṛkāvarṇaiḥ puṭitaṃ mātṛkāsthale | tenaiva puṭitaṃ varṇaṃ nyasettatraiva pārvati ! || iti yāmale —
close_translation: [The Yāmala-citation:] "The praṇava (oṃ) covered (puṭita) by the mātṛkā-letters, in the mātṛkā-site; and the letter covered by that very [praṇava], one should place there, O Pārvatī."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kevalāṃ mātṛkāṃ kṛtvā mātṛkāṃ tārasaṃpuṭām | tāreṇa puṭitāṃ tāntu lajjā tu mātṛkāpuṭā
close_translation: "Having made the bare mātṛkā, [and] the mātṛkā covered-with-the-tāra (oṃ): and that [tāra], covered by the tāra; the lajjā (hriṃ), indeed, the mātṛkā-covered —"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: lajjayā puṭitā sā tu nyastavyā sādhakottamaiḥ | mātṛkayā puṭā yoṣā yoṣayā mātṛkā tathā
close_translation: "And that [tāra], covered by the lajjā, is to be placed by the best of sādhakas; [and] the woman (yoṣā) covered by the mātṛkā, and the mātṛkā by the woman, likewise —"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mātṛkayā puṭaṃ kūrcaṃ kūrcena puṭitārṇatām | mātṛkāpuṭitaṃ cāstaṃ hyastaṃ mātṛkayā tathā
close_translation: "[And] the kūrca (the seed-hriṃ/laṃ), the covering by the mātṛkā; the akṣara (-mass?) covered by the kūrca; and the astra (phaṭ) covered-by-the-mātṛkā, and the astra covered by the mātṛkā, likewise —"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mātṛkāpuṭitaṃ mantraṃ mantreṇa puṭitāntu tām | ayutaṃ vinyased yastu vāyukumbhakayogataḥ || mahāyogī bhavet so'pi devīṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā
close_translation: "The mantra covered-by-the-mātṛkā, and that [mātṛkā] covered-by-the-mantra: he who places the ten-thousand (ayuta, the ayuta-japa) by the breath-binding-yoga (vāyu-kumbhaka), he becomes the great-yogī, and sees the goddess with [his own] eye."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ṣoḍhāhīnasya mantrasya durbalatvaṃ prajāyate | na siddhido bhavet so'pi mokṣado na kadācana
close_translation: "Of the sixfold-less (ṣoḍhā-hīna) mantra, the weakness (durbalatva) is born: it becomes neither the siddhi-giver, nor ever the liberation-giver."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: [the nyāsa-mantra strings] — aṃ tāraṃ aṃ oṃ aṃ namaḥ | oṃ aṃ oṃ namaḥ | strīṃ aṃ strīṃ aṃ namaḥ | strīṃ aṃ strīṃ namaḥ | aṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ | hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ namaḥ | aṃ chaṃ aṃ namaḥ | hūṃ aṃ hūṃ namaḥ | aṃ phaṭ aṃ namaḥ | phaṭ aṃ phaṭ namaḥ | aṃ mūlaṃ aṃ namaḥ | mūlaṃ aṃ mūlaṃ namaḥ | aṃ namaḥ aṃ lajjā aṃ namaḥ lajjā aṃ lajjā namaḥ —
close_translation: [The seventeen nyāsa-mantra strings, transliterated: the varṇa-strings each framed by the praṇava-and-namaḥ (the "aṃ-...-aṃ-namaḥ" formula), covering the tāra, the strīṃ, the hrīṃ, the chaṃ, the hūṃ, the phaṭ, the mūla, and the lajjā — the sixfold placement of the covering-letters on the mantra.]
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: [continued] — aṃ badhūm aṃ namaḥ aṃ kūrcaṃ aṃ namaḥ kūrcaṃ aṃ kūrcaṃ namaḥ | aṃ phaṭ aṃ namaḥ phaṭ aṃ phaṭ namaḥ aṃ mūlaṃ aṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ aṃ mūlaṃ namaḥ iti vāyudhāraṇena nyāsaṃ kṛtvā mūlena saptadhā vyāpakaṃ kuryāt | iti guhyaṣoḍhā —
close_translation: "[continued:] 'aṃ-badhūm-aṃ-namaḥ', 'aṃ-kūrca-aṃ-namaḥ', 'kūrca-aṃ-kūrca-namaḥ', 'aṃ-phaṭ-aṃ-namaḥ', 'phaṭ-aṃ-phaṭ-namaḥ', 'aṃ-mūla-aṃ-namaḥ', 'mūla-aṃ-mūla-namaḥ' — having made the nyāsa with the breath-restraint (vāyu-dhāraṇa), one should make the sevenfold pervasion (vyāpaka) with the root[-mantra]. — thus the secret-sixfold (guhya-ṣoḍhā)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: [the mahā-ṣoḍhā] — hrīṃ aiṃ hauṃ klīṃ huṃ phaṭ | lajjā vāgbhavabījañca prāsādaṃ kāma eva ca | varmabījaṃ tato'pyastraṃ nyastasiddhimavāpnuyāt || iti mahāṣoḍhā —
close_translation: [The great-sixfold (mahā-ṣoḍhā):] "'hrīṃ, aiṃ, hauṃ, klīṃ, huṃ, phaṭ' — the lajjā, the vāgbhava-seed (aiṃ), the prāsāda, the kāma (klīṃ), the varma-seed (hauṃ), and then the astra (phaṭ): placed, one attains the siddhi." — thus the great-sixfold.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: dhūṃ dhūṃ dhūmāvati ! svāhā iti mantraṃ japeddaśa | varṇanyāsakrameṇaiva māyayā puṭitā badhūḥ || badhvā saṃpuṭitān varṇān vinyaset sādhakottamaḥ | ṣaḍdhā nyāsaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mahāsiddhimavāpnuyāt || iti pūrvavat puṭitaṃ kṛtvā varṇanyāsavat pañcāśat sthāne ṣaḍdhā nyaset | iti mahāṣoḍhā —
close_translation: "'dhūṃ, dhūṃ, dhūmāvatī, svāhā' — this mantra one should repeat tenfold; the woman (badhū) covered-by-the-māyā, by-the-letter-nyāsa-order: having covered the letters with the woman (badhū), the best of sādhakas should place [them]; then, having made the sixfold nyāsa, one attains the great-siddhi. — having made the covering as-before, like-the-letter-nyāsa, one should place the sixfold in the fifty (pañcāśat) sites. — thus the great-sixfold."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ kriyate yena ṣoḍhā vatsa ! mahāmahā | mantrasiddhirbhavettasya svapne vākyaṃ śṛṇoti hi
close_translation: "He by whom the sixfold is done every day, O child, the very-great: his is the mantra-siddhi, and he hears the word in [his] dream, indeed."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ṣoḍhā naktaṃ matsyamāṃsaṃ paramānnādibhiryutam | sāyaṃsandhyāṃ tataḥ kṛtvā yogaṃ ca parikalpayet
close_translation: "The sixfold at night, with the fish [and] the flesh (matsya-māṃsa), joined-with-the-supreme-food-and-the-rest: then, having made the evening-saṃdhyā, one should perform the yoga, indeed."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ādhāramūlaṃ grīvāgraṃ merudaṇḍaṃ prakīrtitam | tadāśritya vaset loke koṭitīrthatrayaṃ tanau
close_translation: "The root-of-the-support (ādhāra-mūla, the mūlādhāra) up to the neck's-end: [this] is declared the meru-staff (meru-daṇḍa). Resting on it, one dwells; in the world, the three-fold-koṭi-tīrthas [are] in the body (tanau)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vāme tadaṃśe nāḍī syāt īḍā sarvārthasiddhidā | dakṣiṇe piṅgalā nāḍī sarvatīrthamayī śubhā
close_translation: "At its left part is the channel (nāḍī) the iḍā, the giver-of-all-aims-siddhi; at the right, the channel the piṅgalā, made-of-all-the-tīrthas, auspicious."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: suṣumnā merupurataḥ puṇyanāḍyakhilapradā | tanmadhye citriṇī vajrā tanmadhyataḥ smṛtā
close_translation: "The suṣumnā, before the meru, the giver-of-the-whole pure-channel (puṇya-nāḍī); in its midst [is] the citriṇī; in that [one's] midst, the vajrā, remembered."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: brahmanāḍī samākhyātā brahmānandapradāyinī | indīvaramṛṇāleva rājate madhyamadhyataḥ
close_translation: "[And in its midst] is the brahma-nāḍī, called, the giver-of-the-Brahmā-bliss; like a blue-lotus-stalk (indīvara-mṛṇāla) it shines in the middle-of-the-middle."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sthiravāyusamāyogāttiṣṭhatyeva carācaram | sa tāvat kuṇḍalīśaktirnāsāvāyuḥ prakīrtitaḥ
close_translation: "By the union-with-the-firm-wind, the moving-and-unmoving stands, indeed. That [one] is the kuṇḍalī-power (kuṇḍalī-śakti); the nose-wind (nāsa-vāyu) is declared."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: māyāyogasamāyogāt tatra cāṣṭasthitāni vai | tilakākārarajataṃ tathā bhāti ca tiṣṭhati
close_translation: "By the union-with-the-māyā-yoga, there the eight-stations (aṣṭa-sthita), indeed. The silver (rajata) of-tilaka-form, likewise, shines and stands."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: caitanyarahitā nāḍyo vaddhāstiṣṭhanti dehataḥ | tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ mahāpīṭhaṃ tadāśritya ca tiṣṭhati
close_translation: "The consciousness-less channels (caitanya-rahitā nāḍyaḥ), bound, stand from the body. The tīrtha, the meritorious (puṇya), the great-seat (mahā-pīṭha): resting on it, [it] stands, indeed."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yantraṃ ca devatā tatra mūle ca pariniṣṭhitā | merormūle yathā padmaṃ mūlādhāraṃ prakīrtitam
close_translation: "And the yantra, and the goddess, are there stationed at the root (mūla), indeed. At the meru's-root, as the lotus, the mūlādhāra is declared."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: caturṅgulavistīrṇam ucchritaṃ caturaṅgulam | catuḥparṇaṃ śoṇaparṇaṃ trikoṇaṃ karṇikā tataḥ
close_translation: "Four-fingers broad, raised four-fingers, four-petaled (catuḥ-parṇa), red-leaved (śoṇa-parṇa); then the triangle (trikoṇa), [and] the pistil (karṇikā)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tanmadhye bindurūpohi kākinīśaktisaṃyutā | svayambhū liṅgamākhyātaṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ suśobhanam
close_translation: "In its midst, indeed, the drop-form (bindu-rūpa), joined-with-the-Kākinī-power: the self-born (svayambhū) liṅga, called, golden-colored, very-beautiful."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yavapañcakamānantu mahāliṅgaṃ manoharam | veṣṭayitvā ca viharet śaktiḥ kuṇḍalinī parā
close_translation: "And of-the-five-barley-measure (yava-pañcaka) is the great-liṅga, the charming; having encircled it, the supreme kuṇḍalinī-power plays (viharet)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vilolabhujagākārā brahmarūpavidhāriṇī | sārddhatrivalayākārā mahāyogamayī sadā
close_translation: "Of-restless-serpent-form (vilola-bhujaga-ākārā), bearing-the-Brahmā-form, of-the-one-and-a-half-three-coils-form (sārddha-tri-valaya), made-of-the-great-yoga, always."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ṣaṭpadaiva procyamānā naiva liṅgaṃ spṛśet kvacit | sūryakoṭipratīkāśā candrakoṭisuśītalā
close_translation: "Declared the six-legged (ṣaṭpada, the bee), she never touches the liṅga anywhere; resembling-a-koṭi-suns, cool-with-a-koṭi-moons."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: taḍiccañcalarūpābhā parabrahmasvarūpiṇī | virāṭamūrtirdeveśo viharet pūrvato dale
close_translation: "Of-form-resembling-the-restless-lightning (taḍit-cañcala), of-the-supreme-Brahmā-nature: the Virāṭ-form, the lord-of-gods, plays in the eastern petal (pūrvato dale)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: citkalāśaktisaṃyuktaḥ stūyate ca kṛtāñjaliḥ | mahākālo dakṣiṇe ca kālikāśaktisaṃyutaḥ
close_translation: "Joined-with-the-consciousness-fraction-power (citkalā-śakti), praised, indeed, with joined-hands: the Mahākāla, in the south, joined-with-the-Kālikā-power."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: stayate parayā bhaktyā mahājñānasvarūpiṇīm | nārāyaṇaḥ paścime ca mahālakṣmīkuleśvaraḥ
close_translation: "Praised with the supreme devotion [is] the great-knowledge-formed (mahājñāna-svarūpiṇī): the Nārāyaṇa, in the west, the Mahālakṣmī, the kula-lord."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: stūyate parayā bhaktyā bhāvena kuṇḍalīṃ parām | uttare ca mahādevaḥ pārvatyā saha śaṅkaraḥ
close_translation: "Praised with the supreme devotion, with the bhāva (inner-state), [is] the supreme kuṇḍalī: and the Mahādeva in the north, the Śaṅkara with the Pārvatī."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: stūyate tāriṇīṃ devīṃ sarpākārāṃ maheśvarīm | yadā kadācit tadvācāmekaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇoti hi
close_translation: "Praised [is] the Tāriṇī-goddess, of-serpent-form, the great-mistress. When, at-any-time, one hears the single utterance of their speech, indeed,"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tadā sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiñcāpi saṃhāraṃ kartumeva hi | te śaktāḥ syurmahādeva ! sādhu sādhu prakāśitam
close_translation: "then one is able, indeed, to make the creation (sṛṣṭi), the maintenance (sthiti), and the dissolution (saṃhāra). They are able, O great-god! Well-done, well-done, [it] is revealed."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yadā liṅge bhavelliptā tadā nidrāṃ vrajennaraḥ | sadā sā paramā śaktiḥ sthiralagne sthirā bhavet
close_translation: "When [the kuṇḍalī] becomes smeared (lipta) on the liṅga, then the man goes to sleep (nidrā); always that supreme-power becomes firm in the firm-lagna (the fixed-rising sign)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tadā puṇyakaro loko bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ | yadā mūrdhani liṅgasya sā dadāti sukhaṃ param
close_translation: "Then the world, the merit-doer, will be — no doubt. When, at the head of the liṅga, she gives the supreme ease (sukha):"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: japaśakto bhavet jīvastatra śabde ca siddhidaḥ | yadā pucchaṃ liṅgamūrddhni dadāti brahmarūpiṇī
close_translation: "then the life (jīva) becomes capable-of-japa, and there, in the sound (śabda), the siddhi-giver. When, at the liṅga's-head, the Brahmā-formed [kuṇḍalī] gives the tail (puccha):"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: gurutalpaṃ brahmayoṣāṃ gacchedvālāñca kāminīm | ṣaḍdalaṃ liṅgamūle ca padmaṃ syādraktapāṇḍaram
close_translation: "[then one] would go to the guru's-bed (guru-talpa), the Brahmā-woman (brahma-yoṣā), and the young-desired-woman (vālā kāminī). [For] at the liṅga's-root would be the six-petaled (ṣaḍdala) lotus, red-white (rakta-pāṇḍara)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tanmadhye raktapāṇḍuñca liṅgaṃ viśvodbhavātmikam | hākinīśaktisaṃyuktaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam
close_translation: "And in its midst [is] the red-white liṅga, of-the-universe's-emergence-nature (viśvodbhava-ātmika), joined-with-the-Hākinī-power, the giver-of-all-the-siddhis."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: brahmā viṣṇustathā rudro bhagaścandraḥ śacaupatiḥ | rājate dalamadhye tu sarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ
close_translation: "The Brahmā, the Viṣṇu, and-the-Rudra, the Bhaga, the Candra, the Śacī's-lord (Indra): [they] shine in the petal's-midst, indeed, joined-with-all-the-powers."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: stūyate paramaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvakāmārthasiddhidam | mūlādhārāt kuṇḍalinīṃ tatra yatnena cālayet
close_translation: "The supreme liṅga is praised, the giver-of-all-desire-aims-siddhi. From the mūlādhāra, one should stir (cālayet) the kuṇḍalinī there with effort."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tasyāḥ sparśanamātreṇa dalaṃ tasyottaraṃ mukham | padmopari vrajennaiva mahāśakto maheśvari !
close_translation: "At the mere touch of her, [its] petal [is] her upper-face (uttara-mukha); [and] one should not go above-the-lotus (padmo-pari), O great-power, O Maheśvarī."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kintu tatra sthitāḥ sarve svarvā gacchanti tatkule | ekatrībhūya te sarve stuvanti siddhidāyinīm
close_translation: "But all those standing there go to heaven (svar) in that lineage (tat-kule); becoming-one (ekatrī-bhūya), they all praise the siddhi-giver."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: nābhāvaṣṭadalaṃ padmaṃ navīnajaladaprabham | viśvāntakastatra liṅgaṃ śākinīśaktisaṃyutam
close_translation: "At the navel [is] the eight-petaled (aṣṭa-dala) lotus, of-form-like-the-fresh-cloud (navīna-jalada): the Viśvāntaka there, the liṅga, joined-with-the-Śākinī-power."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: indro vahniḥ pitṛpatirnnair-ṛto varuṇo marut | kuverastatra īśānaḥ svasvaśaktisamanvitaḥ
close_translation: "The Indra, the Vahni (fire), the Pitṛ-pati (the ancestors'-lord), the Nirṛti, the Varuṇa, the Marut (wind); the Kuvera, there, [and] the Īśāna: each-joined-with-his-own-power."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tatra padmasya madhye tu brahmanāḍīsamāśritām | kṛtvā tu tasya pātrāṇi cottarañca vibhāvayet
close_translation: "There, in the lotus's-midst, indeed, having made [the offerings] resting-on-the-brahma-nāḍī, one should contemplate its vessels (pātra) and the north (uttara), indeed."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: te te devāstato gatvā stuvanti bhaktisaṃyutāḥ | hṛdaye ca tato dhyāyet padmaṃ ṣoḍaśabhirdalaiḥ
close_translation: "Those very gods, having gone there, praise, joined-with-devotion. Then, in the heart, one should meditate the lotus with-the-sixteen-petals (ṣoḍaśa-dala)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mahāśuklaṃ mahāpadmaṃ gajakumbhākṛtiṃ dalam | indraścandro guruḥ śukro vāmadevaḥ śivāpatiḥ
close_translation: "The great-white (mahā-śukla), the great-lotus; the petal of-elephant's-temple-form (gaja-kumbhākṛti): the Indra, the Candra, the Guru, the Śukra, the Vāmadeva, the Śiva's-lord (śivā-pati):"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ śaṅkaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ vāmadevaḥ kuleśvaraḥ | kamalānāyakaḥ kopaḥ kāmarūpaḥ kṛpāmayaḥ
close_translation: "the Īśvara, the Śaṅkara, the Kṛṣṇa, the Vāmadeva, the kula-lord (kuleśvara), the Kamalā's-lord, the Kopa (wrath), the Kāmarūpa, the Kṛpāmaya (the merciful):"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: karaṇe ṣoḍaśake ca svasvaṣaktiyoṣāsamanvitaḥ | stūyate sarvadā bhaktyā mahāliṅgaṃ maheśvaram
close_translation: "in the sixteen-faculties (karaṇa), each-joined-with-his-own-power-and-woman (sva-śakti-yoṣā): the great-liṅga, the great-lord, is always praised with devotion."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ḍākinīśaktisaṃyuktaṃ bhāvayecca parātparam | tat panthānaṃ samāruhya tatra devīṃ samānayet
close_translation: "Joined-with-the-Ḍākinī-power, one should contemplate the supreme-and-beyond (parāt-para). Having climbed that path (panthāna), one should bring the goddess there."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tadvāme rājate jīvastadadhaḥ pāpa eva ca | surāpānahṛdā yuktaṃ gurutalpakaṭidvayam
close_translation: "At its left shines the life (jīva); below it, indeed, the sin (pāpa). Joined-with-the-wine-drinking-heart (surāpāna-hṛd): the guru's-bed (guru-talpa), the two-loins (kaṭi-dvaya)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vajradantasamopetaṃ mṛdudantavibhūṣitam | mahākāyaṃ mahādevarahitaṃ hṛdaye sadā
close_translation: "Joined-with-the-vajra-teeth, adorned-with-the-soft-teeth, the great-body, the great-god-devoid (mahādeva-rahita), in the heart always."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: nakhe svarṇahṛtaṃ cihnaṃ sarvadoṣayutaṃ param | navākāraṃ mokṣahīnaṃ kulācāravihīnakam
close_translation: "In the nail [is] the gold-stolen mark (svarṇa-hṛta-cihna), joined-with-all-the-faults, the supreme; the nine-formed (nava-ākāra), the liberation-less (mokṣa-hīna), the kula-conduct-devoid (kulācāra-vihīna)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kāmadaṃ kāmarūpeṇa ratidoṣapradaṃ tathā | tataḥparaṃ bhāvayecca daśapatraṃ suśobhanam
close_translation: "The desire-giving (kāma-da), with-the-desire-form, the rati-fault-giving (rati-doṣa-prada), likewise: then, beyond that, one should contemplate the ten-petaled (daśa-patra), very-beautiful."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: nīlavarṇaṃ mahāpadmaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam | mahāliṅgaṃ kāmanāma rājate kāminīyutam
close_translation: "The blue-colored (nīla-varṇa), the great-lotus, the giver-of-all-the-siddhis: the great-liṅga named the Kāma (desire), shines, joined-with-the-Kāminī."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kāmadevaśca śāmbaśca kāmācāraśca kāmukaḥ | kāminīnāyakaḥ kāmo brahmānandaḥ kuleśvaraḥ
close_translation: "And the Kāmadeva, and the Śāmba, and the Kāmācāra, and the Kāmuka; the Kāminī's-lord, the Kāma, the Brahmānanda, the kula-lord (kuleśvara):"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: trilokeśaḥ sadānandaḥ kaulo daśadale sthitaḥ | svasvaśaktisamopetāḥ stuvanti kuṇḍalīṃ parām
close_translation: "the Trilokeśa, the Sadānanda, the Kaula, standing-in-the-ten-petals: each-joined-with-his-own-power, they praise the supreme kuṇḍalī."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: lalāṭe netrapatrañca brahmaliṅgasamanvitam | saśaktirviṣṇūrudraśca stauti tārāsamanvitaḥ
close_translation: "At the forehead, the eye-petal (netra-patra), joined-with-the-brahma-liṅga; joined-with-power, the Viṣṇu-Rudra, and-[he]-praises, joined-with-the-Tārā."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: taṃ vibhidya gatā devī kuṇḍalī śaktiruttamā | adhomukhaṃ sahasrāraṃ merudaṇḍāgranāḍītaḥ
close_translation: "Having pierced it (vibhidya), the goddess-kuṇḍalī, the supreme-power, goes: the down-faced (adho-mukha) sahasrāra, from the meru-staff's-end-channel (meru-daṇḍa-agra-nāḍī)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: trilokasthāstato devāḥ santi tatraiva śaktibhiḥ | nāḍītrayasamopetaṃ sarojaṃ dvādaśaṃ dalam
close_translation: "The three-world-standing gods, then, are there, indeed, with-the-powers: the lotus joined-with-the-three-channels (nāḍī-traya), the twelve-petaled (dvādaśa-dala)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: trikoṇakarṇikā tatra brahmaviṣṇuśivānvitā | dantāvīkavatī śayyā śaktivajrasamanvitā
close_translation: "The triangle-pistil (trikoṇa-karṇikā) there, joined-with-Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva; the bed of-the-tusked-woman-form (dantāvīkā-vatī), joined-with-the-vajra-power."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tatrāpi śrīguruḥ sākṣāt sarvabhūtahite rataḥ | karpūradhavalaṃ devaṃ brahmarūpiṇamavyayam
close_translation: "There, too, the Śrī-guru, directly, intent-on-the-welfare-of-all-beings: the camphor-white (karpūra-dhavala) god, the Brahmā-formed, the immutable (avyaya)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: paramaṃ śivamākhyātaṃ kauverāsyaṃ vibhāvayet | mūlādidevatāḥ sarve stuvanti sarvakāraṇam
close_translation: "The supreme Śiva-called, of-the-Kuvera-face (kauvera-āsya), one should contemplate; all the root-and-the-rest-goddesses (mūlādi-devatā) praise the all-cause (sarva-kāraṇa)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kuṇḍalinīṃ mahāśaktiṃ lalāṭe kamalāvatīm | bhāvayet śivarūpeṇa vāmabhāge samānayan
close_translation: "The kuṇḍalinī, the great-power, the lotus-possessing (kamalāvatī) at the forehead: one should contemplate in-the-Śiva-form, bringing [her] to-the-left-part (vāma-bhāga)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vāme ratiñca saṃsthāpya guroreva susiddhaye | samutthāya gurustāñca sākārāṃ mantrarūpiṇīm
close_translation: "Placing the rati (pleasure) at the left, for-the-guru's-very-good-siddhi: arising, the guru — she, the formed (sākārā), the mantra-formed (mantra-rūpiṇī)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tatrāpi guruṇā devi! vītaśaktā maheśvarī | upari sthīyate tena mahāmohavināśinī
close_translation: "There, too, by the guru, O Devī, the past-power (vīta-śaktā?), the great-mistress: by that [one] stands above, the destroyer-of-the-great-delusion (mahā-moha-vināśinī). *[X: "vītaśaktā" uncertain — likely a state/epithet of the risen power; the Vṛtti M00323 should settle.]*"
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vāmapādāṅguṣṭhato'syāḥ vakṣyate'mṛtamuttamam | tat pītvā sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ jīvo jīvati nityaśaḥ
close_translation: "From her left-foot's-big-toe (vāma-pāda-aṅguṣṭha) is declared the supreme immortal-nectar (amṛta): drinking that, the life (jīva) lives always, by-ease-and-unease (sukha-duḥkha)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: bhāvanābhyāsayogena yadi nāḍīṃ praveśayet | mahāsiddhiṃ sa labhate'pyamaro jayate dhruvam
close_translation: "By the practice-yoga-of-the-bhāvanā (bhāvanā-abhyāsa-yoga), if one would enter the channel (nāḍī), one gains the great-siddhi; and-the-immortal (amara), one conquers, certainly."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yatrāste kamalā kṛtāñjaliparā vīṇādharā sāradā | tārārādhyamanusmaran priyatamaṃ comāvacaḥ kāraṇam | brahmānandakṛtau susādhanavidhau tārārahasye śubhe | yogācāravidhau caturthapaṭalaḥ sarvārthasiddhipradaḥ
close_translation: "Where stands the Kamalā (Sarasvatī), intent-on-the-joined-hands, holding-the-vīṇā, the Sāradā: remembering the worshipful Tārā, the dearest, the cause of the Umā's-word (umā-vacaḥ) — in the auspicious Tārārahasya of Brahmānanda, in the well-attained-rite (su-sādhana-vidhi), in the yoga-conduct (yogācāra-vidhi), the fourth paṭala, the giver-of-the-success-of-all-aims (sarva-artha-siddhi-prada)."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)
